stories.title: AWS emulator
stories.reason: AWS Emulator: a CC0 local emulator for 200+ AWS services, built end-to-end by AI agents from 400+ Smithy API models and validated against real AWS via agent-written fidelity tests — running code, not a demo, directly addressing the 'agents write code faster than it can be verified' problem.
key_facts: Launched Nov 11 2026; free, offline, CC0 public-domain license
Built from 400+ API models covering 200+ AWS services
Method: agents write end-to-end fidelity tests against real AWS, then build the emulator to pass them
Matt Goldberg's SQS prototype: one prompt to Kiro produced a passable first version in ~15 minutes
Swami Sivasubramanian: a 4-month original engineering effort was rebuilt by an agent in ~2 hours once given a spec and test environment
Merge gate includes adversarial security agents plus a general code reviewer; full commit history and issue tracker public on GitHub

stories.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
stories.reason: Silent Lynx (Kazakhstan-linked) ran an open-source AI agent (Hermes, on DeepSeek, instructed via Telegram in Russian) configured as an 'offensive cybersecurity expert' for recon, data collection and anti-forensics in real intrusions against Tajik, Uzbek and Turkmen government systems — exactly the agent/MCP-style attack-chain-with-real-impact story the profile prioritizes.
key_facts: Threat actor: Silent Lynx / Cavalry Werewolf / YoroTrooper, active since 2022; exposed via a 12GB+ open server found by CloudSEK
AI agent: Hermes (open-source), backed mainly by DeepSeek models, some destructive commands allowed to run without approval
Operator controlled it remotely via a Telegram bot, giving instructions in Russian

Tajikistan: held access to the national railway network Aug-Oct 2026; via one employee's credentials, reached the e-document platform and exfiltrated Defense Ministry, National Guard, and 100+ government orgs' files
Uzbekistan: compromised a server behind the government's Smart Forestry monitoring platform
Turkmenistan: built phishing lures (fake railway ticket, govt report) tested in October; success unknown
Attribution to Kazakhstan is medium-confidence (Russian-language comms, Kazakh ISP test connections), not tied to the government

stories.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
stories.reason: Flagship Gemini 4 Hydrogen launch: 2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash with safety gains (81% less overreach, 2.3x more IPI-resistant) and broad rollout across Search/Gemini/Antigravity.
key_facts: 1M token context, $1.50/$7.50 per M input/output tokens flat across context
Terminal-Bench 4.1: 57% vs 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash
HLE-Diamond 58.8%, Agents' Last Exam v1.1 71.6%
2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash at default thinking level; partners saw 2-2.8x speedups with 12-23% fewer tokens
Overreach down up to 81%, under-service down up to 79%, misaligned/shortcut actions down 12x
2.3x more resilient to indirect prompt injection on Gray Swan IPI benchmark; honesty 96.7%
Rolling out in Gemini API, AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini app, Google Search (all users globally)

stories.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled GPUs
stories.reason: Rigorous independent forensic method (PyTorch Philox RNG seed/thread-count fingerprinting of published weights) identifies five 2026 Chinese frontier models as Blackwell-initialized despite export controls, with results in the 49-1,385 sigma range and validation against 24 disclosed-hardware cases and physical GPU reproduction — real evaluation/provenance methodology with numbers, not a rumor.
key_facts: Method: recovers the Philox RNG seed + GPU thread-count (tied to SM count) that reproduces untouched initial weights
Hopper = 132 SMs/270,336 threads; Blackwell B200/B300 = 148 SMs; GB200/GB300 = 152 SMs
Flagged Blackwell-initialized: DeepSeek-V4-Flash & -Pro, Kimi K3 & K3.1-Pro, MiniMax-M3, Ant's Ling-3.1-flash (all released Apr-Oct 2026)
Strongest per-model result 49-1,385 sigma; chance-match baseline across ~6 trillion seed/layout combos is ~8 sigma
Verified by reproducing weights on real hardware: B300 matched 461/469 DeepSeek-V4-Flash rows; H100 matched all 57,344 preserved DeepSeek-V3 values bit-for-bit
Agreed with all 24 known cases where developers disclosed their training hardware
Author explicitly notes the method can't show how GPU access was obtained or confirm an export-control violation

stories.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
stories.reason: Gemini Decisions API: a new closed-set-scoring endpoint (probabilities/confidence over up to 1000 questions in one multimodal call) that is 5x cheaper than Flash-Lite and gives calibrated confidence scores — a genuine eval/calibration infra story, not just another chat model.
key_facts: Up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice (2-255 options) or rubric-score questions per request, multimodal input up to 256K tokens
150-250ms end-to-end latency, flat from 1 to 100 questions
$0.10 per 1M input tokens, $0 for output tokens (scores options in one forward pass, no generation)
~5x cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite via Interactions API on vendor's benchmark suite
Every answer carries a 0-1 confidence score for routing ambiguous cases to a human/fallback
Gemini Notebook reports up to 40% lower latency using it as a model router

stories.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
stories.reason: IBM's LLMON markup language tags prompt structure explicitly so instructions and data stay separated — on the OPI prompt-injection benchmark it reportedly avoids 47% more attacks than the best frontier model tested and 95% more than the best open model, with models, repo and two papers released.
key_facts: LLMON = LLM Object Notation, an XML-like markup with reserved delimiter tokens binding instructions to specific data spans
OPI prompt-injection benchmark: avoids 47% more attacks than best frontier model, 95% more than best open-source model tested; similar gains on ASB and StruQ
General capability reported on par with base Granite 4.1 Instruct models
Two preview models released: granite-4.1-3b/8b-llmon-preview (not yet production-ready)
Code: github.com/generative-computing/llmon and github.com/generative-computing/mellea (auto-LLMONizes LLM calls)

stories.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
stories.reason: Edge0-145B: open-weight (weights + inference framework released) 145B MoE model (10B active) that beats or matches Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and DeepSeek-V4-Flash on coding/agent benchmarks while running locally in 29GB on a laptop-class GPU.
key_facts: 145B total params, ~10B active per step, shared-expert MoE architecture; sibling Edge0-120B also released
Weights on Hugging Face, inference framework on GitHub (NVFP4 4-bit quantized build)
DeepSWE 1.1: 64.6 vs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 58.7, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 54.4
Terminal-Bench 2.1: 86.52 vs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 83.3, Claude-Opus-4.6 78.2
Mean of six benchmarks: 72.8 vs 71.7 (Qwen) and 70.1 (DeepSeek)
Peak memory 29GB, 80+ tok/s decode, 1,100+ tok/s prefill, ~120W, 128K-256K context
Runs on macOS/Windows/Linux incl. Apple M-series and RTX 4090/5090/Spark

stories.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
stories.reason: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber: a model line explicitly positioned for aligned cybersecurity agents — squarely on the AI x cyber line the profile weights most heavily. Fetch of openai.com was blocked (403); scored on title/source as a primary-source lab announcement.
